Definition: To know — not merely to hold facts but to know by experience, intimacy and covenant relationship.
BiblicalUsage: Yada describes Adam knowing Eve, God knowing Abraham, and the new covenant promise that all 'shall know the Lord.' God desires experiential knowledge of Him more than empty sacrifice.
TheologicalSignificance: Yada is a comfort and an invitation: we are fully known by God, and eternal life is growing to know Him truly — knowledge that is relationship, not just information.
RelatedTopics: Knowledge of God; Covenant; Eternal Life
